claim_decisions.statement: UNICEF–IDMC's September 2025 synthesis describes seasonal Awash flooding in low-lying Afar and Somali communities and substantial drought displacement in conflict-affected Somali and Oromia; it does not apportion the contributions of conflict and weather.

claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2024-11-20 reports: WFP reports that SIIPE expanded from three to 11 Somali Region woredas and reached over 28,000 households by 2021 through subsidized drought livestock insurance, public works and financial-literacy training.
claim_decisions.uncertainty: Region-level programme reach; the 11 woredas are not named in the accessible summary. Delivery is not an effectiveness estimate.

claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2024-11-20 reports: WFP reports complex enrolment, delayed or inadequate payouts, unreliable satellite data, low awareness, capacity gaps, unaffordable premiums and budget shortfalls constrained SIIPE effectiveness and sustainability.

gaps: Historical local studies are not a current conflict map; the 2013–2014 eastern Ethiopia sample was deliberately located in severe drought/conflict areas.
WFP evaluation findings are accessible only as the publisher's substantive summary, not the full estimation tables; positive and null findings are both retained.

executive_assessment.text: Named examples cover Awash lowlands and Doolo/Warder pastoral displacement; historical observations must not be presented as current caseloads.
Eastern Ethiopia respondents perceived drought-related resource pressure within a political and institutional conflict setting; the study does not identify a drought causal effect.
Insurance evaluation findings are mixed, including no demonstrated income, asset or dietary-diversity gains in the publisher summary.
